findings:
🟡 [cost-fuse-dispatch-exempt-single-amp] MUST-FIX `isDispatchBash` (hooks/cost-fuse.js) rejects `;`, `|`, `&&`, backtick, `$(` and newline but not a single `&` followed by another command, nor `<(`/`>(` process substitution. `bash scripts/dispatch-hetero.sh --brief b.md & git push origin x` and `bash scripts/dispatch-hetero.sh --brief <(git push origin x)` both pass the regex (prefix matches, nothing chain-rejected) and are exempted from the fuse in block mode, contradicting the function's own contract ("Anything chained … is not exempt") and test 9c's intent. Impact is bounded (cost-fuse is warn by default, block is opt-in, the model is the actor), but block mode is the one place the exemption matters and it is bypassable with the most common background-chaining operator. Smallest remediation: extend the reject test to `<\(|>\(` and to any `&` that is neither part of a redirect (`2>&1`, `&>`) nor the trailing backgrounding `&` (e.g. reject `/(?<![0-9>])&(?!&|>|\s*$)/` after stripping the match), and add a `& git push` case next to 9c in hooks/tests/cost-fuse.test.sh.
🔵 [cost-fuse-dispatch-path-prefix] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `\S*scripts/dispatch-…` accepts any path prefix (`/tmp/x/scripts/dispatch-evil.sh`), so a non-repo script named like a rail is exempt. Excluded: the hook is a spend guard, not a trust boundary, and the model could equally set `AUTOPILOT_COST_FUSE_MODE=off`; anchoring to the plugin root is optional hardening.
🔵 [cost-fuse-session-id-mismatch] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `sessionSpend` filters ledger rows by raw `payload.session_id` while cost-tracker writes `sanitizeSession(id)`; ids containing characters outside `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` would show `this session $0.00`. Excluded: real session ids are UUIDs and sanitize to themselves; worth a one-line `sanitizeSession` reuse later, not a blocker.
